analysis: Only head-side excerpts of docs/developer/test.md (lines 2691-3565) were supplied, with no patch hunks. They contain documentation only: benchmark, test and CI procedures, with no executable code, coordinator authorization, attestation, encryption or billing change. The text was reviewed against T-041 (prefix-cache / SSD tier, SEC-035). It states that the benchmark runner sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_ROOT and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_PERSISTENT_KEY, and that the root override is ignored without the isolation opt-in. It also describes a persistent test namespace with an access group that forbids ephemeral fallback. These are test-harness controls, and the docs do not claim any change to production defaults. The 30-minute TTL, the HMAC lookup tags, KEK-based purge and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch are not altered in the visible text. Other claims were also checked for conflicts with the threat model, and none conflict: production-grant KV evidence, the e2e testbed env vars, and the docs-impact and commit-signature CI checks. The next pass should confirm that the unseen code changes behind these docs (the ephemeral and test-root env gating in the SSD key loader, and the persistent-test-namespace key selectors) keep the isolation opt-in required, so test overrides cannot activate in production. No such code was in this batch, which is a coverage limit.
